checked.claim: resolveCleanup scores a Tamper with sheet-audit's held stand-in, which has no testUserPermission, so the GM's fresh-scene count reads the whole deaths store and the GM scores 3 lower than the roller's window shows.
checked.why: Read the whole road. resolveCleanup builds held = actorAsHeld(actor) and scores cleanupVerdict(held, ...); cleanupVerdict calls cleanupDc(data.visibility, held), which calls freshSceneBonus({ actor: held }) and so unfoundBodyIn(chapter, undefined, held). actorHeldNow returns a plain object of id, name, type and items, so actor.testUserPermission?.(...) is undefined, players is empty and the filter at 453 never runs: the GM counts its whole deaths store. The number the roller sees is computed with the actor document: cleanableTracesForPlayer (run on the GM through the bridge) gives each row dc = cleanupDc(visibility, actor) with the document, which does filter by knowsOfDeath, and attemptCleanup's dcShown uses that listed dc. So the two numbers differ exactly when an unfound body of this chapter is in the GMs' store, unknown to the roller's player, no incident runs and no discovery stands (config freshScene.onlyWith ['incident','unfoundBody']). No other scorer: grep of cleanupDc( outside tests finds 184, 327, 655 (the roller's own reads, with the document) and 811 (the scorer, with held). The tier-2 V3 test calls C.cleanupDc(visibility, knower) with the fixture document, so it does not read the scorer's argument. Severity kept: it breaks the secrecy rule the 1.2.110 V3 fix was written for, in the ordinary window between an incident's close and the discovery.

Finding 7's confidence moves from suspected to read: its precondition (a victim made a Monocub while Stage 6 still stands after a discovery) is reachable by the code read; severity unchanged.
The Create a Key Remnant here hint is written minor in severity_after: a slot repointed over another GM's placement leaves that token off the plan, which is wrong in a particular situation, not dirt.
not_established: Finding 8's crossing with an action left: a killer whose Tamper menu was opened before their Stage 6 began pays a Sanity mark on their browser and an action on the GM for one attempt (chargeTamper with tamperPriceSkip, then validPrice and chargeUnclaimed). Read, not run; how often the menu stands open across the start of Stage 6 is not measured.
